stories.title: Farage beats Count Binface to win Clacton by-election
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has won the Clacton by-election amid contested claims he was told by police not to attend the election count due to a "credible threat" against him. Mr Farage won with 22,239 votes, with Count Binface in second place on 9,455 votes. Mr Farage secured a 12,784 majority, 62.82% of the vote. This is up from his 8,405 vote majority, 46.2%, when he won at the 2024 general election. The result was declared shortly after 6am. A total of 32 of the record-34 candidates lost their deposit.

stories.title: Rally driver under water for up to six minutes - inquest
stories.summary: A driver whose car veered off track and flipped over into a flooded stream at a forestry rally in Co Kerry, was submerged under water for a period of five to six minutes and had a "very poor prognosis" upon his transfer to hospital, an inquest has heard. Eoin McCarthy from Dunmanway, Co Cork, died during the fourth stage of the Killarney Forestry Rally at Mount Eagle near Castleisland on 20 February 2022. The 22-year-old was driving in his second ever rally alongside navigator Daniel O'Brien when their car veered off a bridge and ended up upside down on its roof in a stream. Dr Fiona Kelly was the chief medical officer on duty at the rally in Castleisland.

stories.title: Parking fee revenue at hospitals doubles over four years
stories.summary: Revenue generated by parking fees at public hospitals has more than doubled over a four-year period. A breakdown provided by the HSE shows that Irish people spent a record €17.76m on car park charges at public and voluntary hospitals in 2025 compared to €7.39m in 2021, representing a 140% increase over a four-year period. The rising figure comes despite a commitment in the Programme for Government last year to "explore further ways to reduce hospital car parking charges". Monies gathered by public and voluntary hospitals from parking fees increased in each subsequent year after 2021, going from €10.61m in 2022 to €13.46m in 2023 and €16.18m in 2024.

stories.title: I-RES sees slight revenue increase, profits jump
stories.summary: Ireland's largest private landlord, Irish Residential Properties REIT (I-RES) has posted its interim results for the first half of the year, saying strong operational and strategic delivery drove earning growth and shareholder returns. The company saw a slight increase in its revenues year on year - it booked €43.1m euro in the six month period, up 1.1 percent on the same period of last year. The group posted a profit before tax of €48 million versus €16.3 million in the prior period. It said this was driven by the non-cash fair value movement of its assets which was underpinned by performance of the portfolio and stable yields.

stories.summary: Two people have been seriously injured after a train with around 150 people on board derailed in southeast England. British Transport Police (BTP) declared a major incident as three carriages derailed on their side, trapping passengers on board the Southern train. The train, which was travelling from London Victoria to Eastbourne, has now been safely evacuated, the force said. Outside a community centre hosting passengers nearby, Yana Ludwig, who was travelling on the train from London to Lewes, told reporters the experience as 2 "completely terrifying".

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.

stories.title: Rovers won't sit back as they chase European league phase
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers are in Albania, looking to close out their third round Europa League qualifier against KF Egnatia and once ensure their participation in European league phase competition. The Hoops take a healthy 3-1 lead into the second after a Graham Burke penalty, a Pico Lopes header, and a goal by Aaron Greene gave them a two-goal advantage in the first leg. Should Rovers be able to see out the tie, they will qualify for the Europa League play-off round where they will face Norwegian side Lillestrom. The winners of that tie will play in the Europa League outright, with the beaten side into the UEFA Conference. Defeat against Egnatia would mean a Conference play-off for Rovers, that's not something they'll be considering after their performance in the first leg.

A talented back who could play scrumhalf or flyhalf, Smith won six caps for the Wallabies in 1987, including at the first World Cup, before moving to Europe to study at Oxford and play nine tests for Ireland. By 1991, his former Wallabies coach ‌Alan Jones had ⁠switched codes and he convinced Smith to join him at the Balmain Tigers rugby league team and he played out his career in the 13-man game in Sydney. After retirement, Smith moved into rugby union coaching ‌and he worked as an assistant under England head coach Martin Johnson from 2008 ⁠to 2011.

stories.title: English strikes gold and Adeleke takes silver at Euros
stories.summary: Mark English has won the gold medal in the men's 800m while Rhasidat Adeleke grabbed silver in the women's 200m at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. Irishman English came home ahead of the rest in 1:45.26 with Croatia's Marino Bloudek second in 1:45.62 and Mohamed Attaqui of Spain third in 1:45.71. The Donegal athlete got away in perfect position, second-over on the outside line behind the front two of Bloudek and Attaqui. stories.title: Civilian casualties in Ukraine highest since 2022 - UN
stories.summary: The number of civilians killed in Ukraine in July jumped to its highest level since the first months of the Russian invasion, the United Nations said, as Moscow intensified its long-range missile strikes. Russia fired a record number of missiles at Ukraine during the month, AFP analysis of data published by Kyiv's air force showed, raining hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles down on the Ukrainian capital. "At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July, a 30% increase compared with the previous month and a 70% increase compared with July 2025," the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission said in a statement. "The number of those killed is the highest recorded since May 2022," it added.

"(With) the likes of Ronan O'Gara who is obviously over in La Rochelle, could he potentially come back? I personally don't see that happening," Madigan explained. stories.summary: Édaein O'Connell, Freelance Journalist, joined Today with David McCullagh to discuss how to debut a new relationship on social media, and whether 'soft launching' it is the way to go. When it came time for O'Connell to reveal a new relationship on her social media, she says she opted for the 'soft launch', the practice of slowly unveiling your new partner online in "drips and drabs". stories.title: €23m spent on Assessment of Need challenges since 2021
stories.summary: The State has spent over €23 million in legal costs arising from Assessments of Need (AON) challenges since 2021, new figures have revealed. Under the Disability Act 2005, parents can take a case against the HSE if they do not receive an assessment report for their child with special needs within a six-month timeframe, if they are unhappy with the outcome of the assessment or if they feel the service was below par. An AON is necessary before a child can start to have their needs met by the State, but there are too few specialists in the system and lengthy waiting lists have become the norm. So far this year, total legal costs for the State stemming from AON challenges amount to €5.6 million, while for the whole of 2025, they totalled €7.2 million.

stories.title: Aviva's first-half profit beats expectations
stories.summary: British insurer Aviva posted a 24% rise in first-half operating profit on Friday, beating expectations, as its combination with Direct Line and growth in general insurance drove earnings higher. Aviva, which offers car, home and life insurance in Britain, Ireland and Canada, has leaned on its diversified model to weather market volatility stoked by the Middle East conflict and softening property and catastrophe rates. CEO Amanda Blanc's £3.7 billion ($4.99 billion) takeover of motor insurer Direct Line, has also proved to be a strong bet for the company, which has seen its sales through price comparison sites surge significantly. Operating profit rose to £1.33 billion for the six months to June 30 from £1.07 billion a year earlier, ahead of the £1.26 billion average forecast in a company-compiled consensus.

stories.title: Under-achieving Derry should take heed of McClean gripes
stories.summary: There is always a tendency, it seems, to focus on how something is said rather than asking the more important question - why was it said in the first place? James McClean has never been someone who keeps his opinion to himself. Derry City knew that when they brought him home in January. Tiernan Lynch spoke about his experience, discipline and ability to raise standards. McClean spoke about wanting to finish his career at Derry and, ideally, deliver the league title the club has waited almost 30 years to win. So nobody can now claim surprise that when McClean felt standards were not where they should be, he said so.

stories.title: McDonald 'couldn't turn down' chance at pro career
stories.summary: Kobe McDonald says he couldn't turn down the opportunity to become a professional athlete in his first interview as a St Kilda player. The 18-year old McDonald, son of former Mayo great Ciaran McDonald, was one of the stories of the inter-county season as he made a rapid adjustment to inter-county football and then helped the county deliver a sensational and unexpected All-Ireland final victory amid euphoric scenes at Croke Park. A further element to the story was the knowledge all the while that McDonald was bound for Aussie Rules, having agreed to join St Kilda once he'd completed his leaving cert, which he did during the summer. "I've always dreamed of being a professional athlete," McDonald told St Kilda's YouTube channel.
